newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch consider Shell plan to reduce CO2 emissions.
newsitem.headline: Dutch consider Shell plan to reduce CO2 emissions.

text.p: The Dutch environment ministry said on Friday it was discussing with Royal Dutch/Shell Group the possibility of injecting carbon dioxide (CO2) produced at Shell's Pernis refinery into the ground.

The possibility comes as Shell brings its "Per+" project on stream in June. The new units are capable of extracting up to a million tonnes of carbon dioxide per year. The gas could then be pumped into an old gas reservoir.
The plan, if carried out, would curb emissions of the greenhouse gas which the Dutch government wishes to reduce to three percent below 1990 levels by the year 2000.
Economic growth in the Netherlands has led to a seven percent increase so far this decade, with one percent representing about 1.7 million tonnes, an environment ministry spokesman said.

"We are looking at all possibilities to reduce carbon dioxide emissions, but obviously they cost a lot of money. We are discussing this plan with Shell, but no decision has been taken yet," the spokesman said, adding a decision should be reached within a matter of months.
The Dutch government has set aside 1.5 billion guilders ($782.6 million) since last year to tackle rising carbon dioxide emissions.
Shell itself expresses a preference for piping the gas to nearby greenhouses where carbon dioxide is used to stimulate plant growth.
"We prefer this option, because the gas is used. However, we are at a very premature stage," said spokesman Maarten Broekers of Shell Netherlands.
The announcement comes in the same week that Shell published its first ever company-wide environmental report which showed emission levels at its plants have been relatively stable.
-- Philip Blenkinsop, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5004 ($ = 1.916 Dutch Guilders)
